reading.body:
CyrusOne's Cincinnati facility publishes 11 MW of IT capacity across 143,778 square feet, making it the third-largest disclosed data center in Ohio and holding 18 percent of the state's declared 60.4 MW.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this footprint translates to roughly 275 racks. The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government sectors. Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities on record, but only eight publish IT capacity figures, so CIN2 is among the rare transparent sites in the state.

Ohio's total published capacity of 60.4 MW places it at the lower end of AI infrastructure density compared to major compute hubs. Whether this reflects actual scarcity or merely undisclosed capacity is unknown. The state's grid and power supply have not yet appeared as visible constraints in published facility announcements, suggesting either surplus availability or an absence of large-scale AI training demand seeking Ohio capacity.

For an operator needing east-of-Mississippi compliance-ready infrastructure, 11 MW is neither hyperscale nor negligible. It is sufficient for a mid-tier training cluster or inference workload, but the modest regional capacity signals that Ohio remains peripheral to the geography of large-scale compute concentration.
